scope: Planning judgments for the mapped selected-package procedures; not new compilation or numerical verification.

benefit_review.assessment: Routine gap-filling batches now have diminishing benefit: the remaining mapped records mostly contain retained failures, sandbox limits or overlapping class claims. Do not add duplicate variants merely to reach ten drivers.
benefit_review.latest_batch: Five separately reviewed scientific-table APIs remain worthwhile: logarithmic interpolation, logarithmic integration and cumulative prefixes, conservative rebinning, bilinear interpolation and masked histograms. See docs/gams-fortranlib-tables.md. These are new capabilities, not evidence that the full package API inventory has been exhausted.
benefit_review.recommendation: Pause automatic gap-filling batches. Prefer named new APIs with independent oracles, common problems comparing multiple packages, resolving the PCA linking limit, or retesting an upstream repair. Review each proposed batch for distinct mathematical coverage before implementation.

unchecked_procedures.notes: Scientific utilities. The main sorts repeated and negative integers, builds a k-d tree for 20 deterministic 2D points and compares the nearest point with an independent direct search. The OpenMP metapackage is resolved explicitly and -fopenmp is enabled; the execution sandbox still uses one thread. No source edits. The broad library is compiled, but this driver does not validate all containers, random generators, mathematical utilities or parallel performance. A broader nearest-neighbor probe fails on a valid 31-point query; its source, hash and result are retained in docs/gams-candidates/coretran-nearest. This procedure has no checked GAMS driver.
unchecked_procedures.action: Retain the valid 31-point failing query; repeat full brute-force nearest-neighbor checks after a repair rather than promote the small ordinary smoke test.

unchecked_procedures.notes: The existing upstream FPM package is compiled against pinned PLplot native libraries and the Cairo file driver. The main plots sine and cosine over [0,2*pi] using the pngcairo device, checks that the output file exists and is nontrivial, and the restricted sandbox must return a valid PNG preview for browser display. GUI devices, animation, interactive windows and other plotting routines are outside verification scope. Q describes the tested graphics functionality.
unchecked_procedures.action: Reuse the headless author-style plotting setup, then add independent source-data/axis checks and artifact validation. A nonempty PNG alone is not mathematical verification.

unchecked_procedures.notes: 48 dyadic uniform-grid cubic samples, lengths 5..20 and h=1/8,1/4,1/2. First, second and third forward difference quotients checked with exact polynomial formulas; first-difference cumulative reconstruction checked. Not a general derivative-error estimator or integration quadrature. Combined probe failed cumulative reconstruction: 4.458984375 instead of 4.486328125. cumsum sorts before prefix summation; full probe retained. Not a checked cumsum API.
unchecked_procedures.action: The difference-only API already has a checked driver. Resolve or clarify cumsum's sorting behavior before claiming ordered prefix sums; do not add another diff duplicate.

unchecked_procedures.notes: 99 finite REAL32 data sets n=1..33. Median and seven scalar/vector percentiles checked against an independent sorted-data reference using plotting positions (i-1/2)/n and endpoint clamping. Integer percentile API only; other quantile conventions excluded. Built but crashed with SIGSEGV at the first median call for n=1; retained exact probe and output. No median or percentile driver published.
unchecked_procedures.action: Diagnose the first n=1 median crash. Percentile-only testing could be a separately reviewed consumer because the failed combined probe did not reach it.

unchecked_procedures.notes: SVD-based principal directions and covariance analysis; D6 and L13b remain source-supported. See docs/gams-candidates/forpca/covariance-variances-result.json and docs/gams-sparse-integral.md. The ordinary catalog demo checks direction and an independently formed rank-one reconstruction only; no checked PCA variance driver is published.
unchecked_procedures.action: Keep the wrong-variance reproducer. Recheck an upstream repair or separately reviewed mode; do not reduce assertions to direction-only checks and call PCA variances verified.

unchecked_procedures.notes: Uniform real test arrays generated from RANDOM_NUMBER; assertion routines are separate software-testing tools. unchecked_procedures.notes: The original gtk-fortran 4.8.0 FPM manifest is unchanged and builds the core bindings and high-level helper modules. additional_class_claims.notes: Mimetic vector-calculus library with pinned Julienne and Assert dependencies. A single-image coarray build is used. The checked consumer adapts the author's extended Gauss-divergence example to f=x**2/2 and v=x on a 64-cell unit interval. It checks the two volume integrals against 1/3 and 1/6, the boundary flux against 1/2, finiteness and the conservation residual using single-precision tolerances. The command-line parsing and shell display calls of the upstream example are omitted. Library numerical sources are unchanged. Other 2D/3D operators, time integration and convergence orders are not validated. Original Berkeley Lab license terms, including the enhancements clause, are retained; this is not labeled plain BSD-3-Clause.
additional_class_claims.action: H1 divergence/gradient success is not a time-dependent PDE solution. Split volume-integration and PDE claims; I2 needs a real evolution/boundary problem, not relabeling the operator test.

additional_class_claims.notes: Native Fortran FMM2D source set selected from the upstream makefile with optional C++ fast kernels disabled. OpenMP and portable -O2 are enabled; the visitor sandbox uses one execution thread and retains bounds checks. Checksum-guarded compatibility edits skip zero-point multipole/local evaluations and zero-source neighbor calls before passing one-past-end array elements. The inverse reorder helper declares its arrays with the actual n extent rather than the legacy dummy extent 1. Source and target branches receive matching guards; formulas are unchanged. The checked real Laplace driver evaluates 512 deterministic sources at 16 separate targets and compares with an independent charge-weighted log-distance sum. A separate source-and-target probe also checks all source potentials by direct summation with self-interactions excluded, exercising the source-side guards. The code is classified as a structured kernel-matrix application and Green-function evaluation related to PDEs, not as a complete boundary-value solver. Helmholtz, biharmonic/Stokes, dipoles, gradients/Hessians, every complex/vector interface and parallel speedups are not validated. The small accuracy check is not a performance benchmark.
additional_class_claims.action: Review whether this is a distinct algorithm/configuration, a supporting capability already exercised, or an overly broad discovery claim. Do not duplicate or relabel a driver automatically.

additional_class_claims.notes: Xoroshiro128+ pseudo-random generator. An FPM wrapper selects unchanged m_random.f90 and uses -fwrapv for its intentional signed-integer wraparound. Two fresh generators replay 10000 seeded uniform draws exactly; the main checks the implementation range [0,1), broad uniform/normal/Poisson(4) moment tolerances, nonnegative counts and unit circle/sphere norms. These are deterministic smoke checks, not statistical quality or cryptographic validation. OpenMP, jump independence, large Poisson rates and all distributions are not covered. A separate hosted reproducer confirms that set_seed does not clear the cached second normal after an odd normal() call; use a fresh generator to restart normal sequences. The selected replay uses fresh objects. Dedicated L6a21 driver checks 15 interleaved streams against unsigned-Python prefixes and rolling hashes, exact 52-bit integer/uniform conversion, seeded restarts and zero/default/two explicit jumps. Jump references use independent GF(2) transition-matrix exponentiation to 2**64. This establishes fixed bitstream and seed/jump API behavior, not statistical quality or thread independence; the cached-normal reseeding defect remains unresolved.
additional_class_claims.action: Existing golden-stream driver already checks seed/jump behavior. Review whether to expose that proof under L6c before writing a duplicate; cached-normal reseeding remains a separate retained failure.
